editorial:
Imagine a group of free-spirited hippies packing up their van for a music festival, only to find out they are being hunted by a killer who absolutely hates their lifestyle. The bad guy is a weirdo who is obsessed with Ronald Reagan and wants to clean up the world by getting rid of anyone who doesn't fit his old-school view of America. It is a wild ride that blends silly humor with blood and guts, making it feel like a total B-movie party. You get a mix of bright colors, loud music, and a killer who is just as strange as the people he is chasing.

What really makes this work is how it doesn't take itself too seriously. The acting is campy and the kills are over the top, though some parts of the story move a bit slower than others. If you love movies that make fun of horror tropes, you will have a blast. It is the perfect flick to put on during a movie night with friends. Since it is an older low-budget movie, you might want to look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your collection for the best quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick laugh.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a final showdown where the survivors fight back against the Reagan-loving killer. After a chaotic struggle, the killer is finally defeated in a messy and ironic way that fits the movie's dark humor. The remaining hippies manage to escape the nightmare, though they are definitely scarred for life. It ends on a light note, showing that the weirdos won over the hateful killer in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy horror movies and dark comedy.
